previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted for elective placement of a left arm AV loop graft. Due to vessel calcification, a PTFE graft was placed successfully. She was monitored overnight for hand ischemia and neuropathy symptoms, which remained stable. She received hemodialysis via her existing tunneled catheter and was discharged home the following day with instructions to monitor graft function, avoid venipuncture or blood pressure measurements in the left arm, and follow up with the access clinic. No complications were observed during the admission.

>> ACTIVE ISSUES
# Left upper extremity cellulitis: She presented with swelling, 
tenderness, erythema and dried purulence at the site of her left 
arm AV loop graft placed one week prior to admission. She was 
placed on Vancomycin on admission, which was subsequently dosed 
with HD. Her cellulitis improved. She had a downtrending WBC 
count and remained afebrile. Her pain was well controlled with 
APAP. No active purulence was observed. The arm became less 
tender. She was transitioned to PO doxycycline to complete a 7 
day course of antibiotics. She was educated about the most 
common side effects associated with doxycycline included pill 
esophagitis and photosensitivity. 
.
# AV loop graft. She was seen by transplant surgery while in the 
hospital. There was concern for radial steel syndrome in the L 
extremity given the status of the graft. No operative 
intervention was deemed necessary while inpatient. She was to 
follow up in transplant clinic on ___ for further evaluation 
and possible fistula ligation. 
.
# Diarrhea: The patient presented with 2 days of diarrhea in the 
setting of ___ days of constipation. She had been taking 
dilaudid since discharge for her fistual on ___. On admission, 
she underwent KUB, which demonstrated a large stool burden 
without obstruction. The diarrhea prior to admission was thought 
to be due to overflow, in the setting of constipation likely due 
to opioid use and decreased gut motility at baseline. She was 
placed on an aggressive bowel regimen. She continued to have 
several loose stools/day. She was C. diff negative. She denied 
abdominal pain on the day of discharge. She was not prescribed 
any opioids on discharge. She was cautioned about the risk of 
constipation with opioid use and need for regular use of bowel 
regimen.  
.

gastroparesis):  She was placed on her home regimen of NPH 35 at 
breakfast and 5U dinner. She refused the 5 units NPH at dinner

was placed on her home ISS for prandial. Her blood sugars were 
mildly well controlled 100-200s.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with recent dilaudid use post surgery, with
constipation that turned into diarrhea. Concern for overflow diarrhea.  //
Please evaluate for degree of stool in intestines

TECHNIQUE:  Supine and left lateral decubitus abdominal radiographs were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiographs dated ___.
CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is a central venous catheter with the tip in the right atrium, which
appears unchanged in comparison to the prior chest radiograph.  There are
median sternotomy wires which also appear unchanged.  Also noted are vascular
clips consistent with prior cardiac surgery.  The lung bases are clear
bilaterally.

There is a large amount of stool seen throughout the colon.  The bowel gas
pattern is unremarkable with gas seen in nondistended loops of large and small
bowel. There is no evidence of ileus or obstruction. There is no evidence of
intraperitoneal free air on the left lateral decubitus view. The bony
structures are unremarkable.  There is severe atherosclerosis of the abdominal
aorta and the iliac vessels.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Large amount of stool seen throughout colon.
2.  Non-obstructive bowel gas pattern.
